subject: Request: regional approvals & localization plan for Eurasoft + NipponAI reference
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Marta Sokol <m.sokol@eurasoft.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 14:01:00 +0000
Subject: Request: quick approvals for a short case study (localization items)

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the product feedback last quarter; the Eurasoft team has been a great partner. We put together a short draft case study that highlights the latency/cost wins you saw after moving inference to Redwood Dedicated. Would Eurasoft be open to being a short customer reference?

Two quick asks if yes:
- Permission to publish a 1–2 page case study and 1–minute quote we can use in marketing (we’ll send drafts).
- Signoff on localized versions for German and Polish (we’d handle translation and would like your legal/comms to review).

We’ll keep it high-level and can include any redactions you prefer. If it helps, I can share the English draft and a localization checklist this week.

Open to a 20-min call if you prefer to walk through.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_case_draft_en.docx (draft)

From: Marta Sokol <m.sokol@eurasoft.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:18:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: quick approvals for a short case study (localization items)

Hi Markus —

Thanks for sending this over. Eurasoft is fine in principle, but two things from our side:
1) Any customer quote needs approval from Legal (we route standard releases through our comms/legal).
2) For Germany/Poland translations, our local teams prefer we review wording to ensure accurate product claims in each language.

Can you confirm: will Redwood provide the translated copy for review (we don’t want to re-translate internally), and do you have a short checklist for regional compliance we can use?

If yes, please send both and I’ll route to Legal and the DE/PL product owners. We can aim to close approvals by next Friday (24th) if timelines are short.

Best regards,
Marta
Head of Partnerships, Eurasoft

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Request: quick approvals for a short case study (localization items)

Team — forwarding Eurasoft’s reply. Key asks: legal approval path and translated copy for DE/PL to review.

Marissa — can you own the translation handoff and provide the localization checklist?
Vivek — Laura flagged that Eurasoft may ask for data residency language in the German version; can Legal/Compliance draft a short paragraph we can include (and translate) quickly?

I’ll propose a 20-min call with Marta and the local product owners on Thursday to speed approvals.

Thanks,
Markus

To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: quick approvals for a short case study (localization items)

Thanks Markus — I can take this. Plan:
1) I’ll produce German and Polish translated drafts (Redwood-managed translators) and upload to the Drive link.
2) I’ll attach a short localization checklist (naming conventions, regulatory claims, metrics rounding rules) so local PO/legal can sign off faster.
3) Suggest we include two short legal blurbs: a) standard data residency statement for EU customers, and b) non-endorsement language. Laura — can you draft those blurbs?

I also want to flag APAC nuance — we’ve been doing short references in Japan where product names and honorifics are sensitive. If we plan a NipponAI reference later (Kenji copied on the thread I’ll add), we should surface those nuances now.

Proposed timesheet: translations & checklist by EOD Thursday (17th), then 48-hour review from Eurasoft local teams.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Marketing Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: localization_playbook_v1.pdf

From: Marta Sokol <m.sokol@eurasoft.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 09:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: quick approvals for a short case study (localization items)

Hi all —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. I reviewed the plan with Legal and the DE/PL product leads. They’re OK with Redwood-provided translations and the checklist — two small asks before sign-off:

1) Please include a single-sentence data residency note specific to our EU contracts (example attached in reply below).
2) For the German text, avoid any comparative language on latency without a clear benchmark (they want: "up to X%" rather than absolute statements).

We can approve the German and Polish drafts within 48 hours after you upload them. After that, we’ll provide a short quote and a one-paragraph case headline.

Also, Markus — you mentioned NipponAI earlier. Kenji is open to being a reference but will require a slightly different doc flow (native Japanese copy first, then English). If/when we reach out to Kenji, please copy me — Eurasoft can help coordinate (we operate in both regions).

Best,
Marta

Attachment stub: example_data_residency_clause.txt
